items.title: The PERFECT FPL Wildcard Team for GW4
items.headline: Gonzalo over Wissa anchors Dan’s Gameweek 4 Wildcard rebuild
items.summary:
Dan activates his Wildcard in Gameweek 4 to turn a collection of short-term punts, poor fixtures and uncertain starters into a durable squad intended to need no planned transfers until at least Gameweek 8. His previous side carries difficult runs for Manchester United and Sunderland defenders, unwanted Coventry assets from a Gameweek 2 Bench Boost, and unstable Manchester City midfield options such as Cherki. The objective is a “robust” 15-man squad with playable bench cover, allowing free transfers to accumulate for injuries, form shifts and the international break rather than being spent on fixture-driven repairs.

The first draft starts Kinsky in goal, with Spurs preferred to the other £4.5m keepers. Arsenal’s David Raya is viewed as the standout premium goalkeeper, but the gap between the remaining premium options and cheap starters is not considered worth the extra spend. Kinsky’s home fixtures against Everton, Aston Villa, Coventry and Crystal Palace are attractive, while Spurs are expected to become a stronger defence than Brighton, Bournemouth, Fulham or Hull. The defence contains Arsenal pair Calafiori and Concer, with Calafiori established as an attacking, first-choice left-back and Concer expected to cover the injured Saliba until at least December. Vuskovic and Maharovic are selected for defensive-contribution potential and aerial threat, while Lewis Hall offers Newcastle clean-sheet, set-piece and rotation value from the bench.

Cole Palmer, Bukayo Saka, Szoboszlai and Pascal Gross make up the midfield behind Erling Haaland and Joao Pedro. Palmer is the leading Gameweek 4 captain against Hull, supported by his form, penalties and greater set-piece responsibility. Saka’s strong minutes and potentially improved penalty access make him a premium Arsenal priority. Szoboszlai is preferred to Gakpo because Gakpo’s minutes may become less secure as Liverpool’s new options settle in, despite Gakpo’s recent returns; Szoboszlai’s underlying shooting numbers remain encouraging. Gross is a functional £5.5m enabler with penalties, corners and free-kicks, and can be benched for Arsenal.

The key forward call is Gonzalo over Wissa. Gonzalo has 11 shots and 1.45 non-penalty xG in three matches, plays 90 minutes and may inherit Fulham penalties. Although Liverpool are first up, Manchester United’s openness is seen as exploitable before Ipswich, Hull and Coventry provide a three-game promoted-team run. Wissa is rejected because Newcastle’s chance creation has been limited, he has dropped deep, and the returns of Oscela and Fernandez Pardo could threaten both his role and minutes. Tavernier currently fills the final midfield spot after Sangare is substituted at half-time and Garner suffers an injury, but Dan identifies the Bournemouth midfielder as the least secure selection despite his strong xG, near-DefCon output, set pieces and possible penalty involvement.
key_points: Cole Palmer is the preferred Gameweek 4 captain at home to Hull, with Haaland and Saka providing premium alternatives.
Kinsky is selected as a £4.5m goalkeeper because Spurs’ fixture run is strong and non-Raya premium keepers do not justify their price.
Calafiori and Concer form a double Arsenal defence, with Concer expected to benefit from Saliba’s long absence.
Vuskovic and Maharovic are long-term defensive picks for DefCon points, set-piece threat and the ability to return even without clean sheets.
Gonzalo is chosen over Wissa after strong early shot and xG numbers, secure 90-minute appearances and Fulham’s favourable run from Gameweek 5 onward.
Lewis Hall is a valuable rotation defender for Newcastle’s upcoming fixtures and is preferred to Livramento due to his stronger role and set-piece access.
Tavernier is the most tentative Wildcard pick; his attacking numbers and set pieces appeal, but he could be replaced before the deadline.
The squad is built to roll transfers after the Wildcard, potentially reaching five free transfers by Gameweek 8 rather than booking immediate moves.

items.title: My FPL GW4 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ MY GAMEWEEK 4 TEAM 🎯
items.headline: Palmer is the Gameweek 4 captain as Chelsea’s Hull fixture outweighs Haaland’s United appeal
items.summary:
Gameweek 3 produces an unusually low-scoring round for many popular FPL assets, with Haaland, Isak and Sesko the only forwards to score. Haaland’s nine-point return against Coventry is respectable but underwhelming for the many managers who use Triple Captain, while Isak punishes wildcard sellers with a goal against Ipswich. Mbeumo also returns immediately after being the most-sold player, while Bruno Fernandes, Foden, Cherki and Thiago blank. Thiago remains a sell despite 2.4 xG without a goal, as Brentford’s fixtures worsen from Gameweek 4.

The priority move for Gameweek 4 is Foden to Cole Palmer, with Palmer taking the captaincy at home to Hull and João Pedro vice-captain. Hull have somehow kept three consecutive clean sheets, but have conceded more than five expected goals and are unlikely to sustain that record against Chelsea. Haaland remains a strong alternative captain against Manchester United, particularly given his record in that fixture, but City’s attacking rotation makes most of their midfielders unattractive. Semenyo and Enzo are the safer City midfield considerations, while Anderson is viewed as their best long-term value option.

A wildcard side can plausibly go without Haaland in Gameweek 4 to accommodate Palmer, João Pedro and premium Arsenal options, although it is a high-risk call. Arsenal offer exceptional depth: Raya is a leading goalkeeper option, Gabriel and Calafiori carry set-piece and attacking appeal, Ødegaard has two double-digit returns in three matches at £6.6m, and Saka, Rice and Havertz all remain viable. Chelsea’s Palmer and João Pedro are considered holds rather than short-term punts, despite Arsenal beating Chelsea 2-1 in Gameweek 3.

The proposed Gameweek 4 XI is Raya; Van Hecke, De Cuyper and Konsa; Saka, Foden, Szoboszlai and Groß; Haaland, Wissa and João Pedro, with £3.3m deliberately held back to fund Foden to Palmer. Retaining budget after that switch preserves defensive flexibility: a fifth-defender slot is kept cheap with Mendy rather than spending on Djed Spence or Ajer, leaving funds to upgrade Konsa or De Cuyper to the stronger £5m-plus defender pool. Bournemouth defenders, particularly Silva, become targets from Gameweek 7 when their schedule improves, while De Cuyper can cover the short term before a potential switch.
key_points: Transfer Foden to Cole Palmer for Gameweek 4 and captain Palmer at home to Hull; João Pedro is the preferred vice-captain.
Haaland is still a credible captain against Manchester United, but nine points from his Coventry match is only a middling Triple Captain outcome.
Avoid most Manchester City attackers because of rotation risk, with Anderson the standout longer-term midfield value and Semenyo or Enzo safer alternatives.
Ødegaard is emerging as a £6.6m Arsenal bargain after two double-digit returns in his first three matches, while Raya, Gabriel, Calafiori, Saka and Havertz offer competing Arsenal routes.
Sell Thiago despite his underlying 2.4 xG, as Brentford move into Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool fixtures.
Djed Spence has significant attacking upside but carries longer-term selection and defensive risk, with Livramento having already been benched.
Target Bournemouth defenders from Gameweek 7, when Sunderland at home begins a favourable run; Silva is a leading £5m option.
Keep cash in reserve rather than over-investing in a fifth defender, as the £5m-plus defensive bracket offers far better replacement options than the £4.5m tier.

items.title: 3x TRANSFERS CONFIRMED! OR WILDCARD? ♻️ MY FPL GW4 TRANSFER PLANS 📝 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Palmer and Gibbs-White moves allow Gameweek 6 Wildcard wait
items.summary:
Three transfers are already confirmed for Gameweek 4: Bruno Fernandes makes way for Cole Palmer ahead of Chelsea’s home match with Hull, Solanke is upgraded to Morgan Gibbs-White, and Rodon is sold for Muharemovic. Palmer is preferred despite Hull’s clean-sheet start because their underlying defensive numbers remain poor and Chelsea are creating chances; Gibbs-White appeals as Nottingham Forest’s set-piece and penalty taker, as well as their main open-play threat, for Aston Villa, Coventry and Crystal Palace. Muharemovic is chosen partly to avoid Rodon’s price fall and offers DefCon and attacking appeal against Newcastle and Crystal Palace, although Ben White and Ezri Konsa were considered.

The current squad is viewed as strong enough to avoid an immediate chip. Verbruggen is marginally preferred over Kinsky in goal, away at Coventry rather than at home to Everton, while the key outfield dilemma is whether to start Brighton’s Gomez at Coventry or Bryan Mbeumo against Manchester City. Gomez has the fixture and a full midweek rest, but Mbeumo’s quality and City’s tendency to concede chances make him difficult to bench. Szoboszlai is a concern because of limited attacking output and occasional right-back minutes, but Fulham at home keeps him in the side for now. João Pedro, Calvert-Lewin and Erling Haaland lead the line, with either João Pedro or Palmer set to be captain.

European fixtures raise fresh rotation and injury risks, with Aston Villa and Manchester City playing in the Champions League on Tuesday, Liverpool and Arsenal on Wednesday, and Manchester United on Thursday. That makes waiting on transfers advisable where possible. Palmer is the preferred short-term Chelsea midfield target for Hull at home because his penalties and explosive ceiling outweigh Morgan Rogers’ value appeal, while João Pedro is considered the standout Chelsea attacker overall. A Chelsea attacking triple-up is viable, especially with no European schedule, but two Chelsea attackers is the likely standard approach.

A Gameweek 4 Wildcard would feature Raya, Calafiori and Konsa in defence, plus Palmer, Gibbs-White, Pascal Gross and Mbeumo behind Wissa, João Pedro and Haaland. However, it may overcommit to lower-upside defenders and make a later move for Bukayo Saka or Martin Ødegaard awkward. A Free Hit would aggressively target Chelsea against Hull, Brighton at Coventry, Arsenal against Fulham and Liverpool against Sunderland, with options including Saka, Palmer, Rogers, Gakpo, Alexander Isak and João Pedro. For now, neither chip is planned: the squad projects well for both Gameweeks 4 and 5, allowing a transfer roll in Gameweek 5 and a planned Wildcard in Gameweek 6 over the international break. A significant midweek injury, mounting price-loss concerns or fear of missing Arsenal and Isak could still trigger a chip.
key_points: Cole Palmer, Morgan Gibbs-White and Muharemovic are the three confirmed transfers in for Gameweek 4, replacing Bruno Fernandes, Solanke and Rodon.
Captaincy is a close call between João Pedro and Palmer, with Palmer’s penalty role and haul potential strengthening his case against Hull.
Start Verbruggen over Kinsky is the current goalkeeper call, while Gomez versus Mbeumo is the main outfield benching decision.
João Pedro is rated the best Chelsea attacker, while Palmer is favoured over Morgan Rogers for the immediate Hull fixture because of his greater explosive upside.
European matches for Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United create rotation and injury risks, so late-week reassessment is important.
The preferred chip plan is to roll in Gameweek 5 and Wildcard in Gameweek 6; a midweek injury is the likeliest reason to bring that Wildcard forward.
A Free Hit would load up on Chelsea, Brighton, Arsenal and Liverpool assets, but it is currently considered unnecessary because the existing squad has strong Gameweek 4 and 5 coverage.

items.title: Transfer tonight 🤔 Cherki 👉 Rogers ✅ FPL Gameweek 4 Early Thoughts 🔥
items.headline: Morgan Rogers becomes the priority as Cherki’s Manchester City minutes look fragile
items.summary:
Morgan Rogers is the standout Gameweek 4 transfer target, with a move from Rayan Cherki to Rogers planned to exploit Chelsea’s home fixture against Hull and a favourable longer run. Rogers offers dependable starts and strong durability, while Cherki’s 65-minute outing underlines the risk of Manchester City’s crowded attack. Cherki starts ahead of Phil Foden in the No. 10 role, but with Semenyo, Iliman Ndiaye and eventually Doku competing for wide roles, neither Cherki nor Foden looks secure for 90 minutes. Foden is the clearer sell after being benched, although Champions League team news should be checked first; Cherki is a less urgent exit and can be held for Sunderland at home in Gameweek 5 if managers want to save a transfer.

The proposed squad move is Cherki to Rogers, despite the risk of Chelsea’s midweek Carabao Cup tie against Leeds. Rogers is close to a price rise, and the transfer creates a three-man Chelsea attack alongside Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro for Hull at home. The argument is simple: all three are individually strong picks with reliable league minutes and Chelsea’s fixtures remain attractive after Gameweek 4, including Brentford away, Bournemouth at home, Everton away and Manchester United at home. Erling Haaland remains the captaincy focus for Gameweeks 5 and 7, while Joao Pedro is also a premium Gameweek 4 option against Hull.

Manchester United midfielders Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are not forced sales despite facing Manchester City at home. Fernandes hits the bar against Everton and Mbeumo scores again, while both remain likely to play heavy minutes and have a solid run after Gameweek 4: Fulham away, Spurs at home, Leeds away and Bournemouth at home. However, moving Mbeumo to Rogers or Fernandes to Palmer is a reasonable higher-upside play, particularly for managers with a Wildcard available to reverse the decision later.

At the back, Nico O’Reilly’s warm-up injury requires patience rather than an immediate sale. If he is likely to return for Sunderland in Gameweek 5, benching him for Manchester United is viable, especially as a City clean sheet is not expected. If he is ruled out longer term, Josko Gvardiol at £5.6m gains appeal, although neither City defender is an urgent buy. Arsenal’s Kiwior is a stronger budget option at £4.4m while Mosquera is absent, with a probable run at right centre-back beside Gabriel. For other replacements, Van Hecke at £4.9m and Leeds’ Mahamovic are preferred value defenders, while Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk is less appealing given a difficult fixture stretch and uncertain clean sheets.

Hull’s three clean sheets should not deter investment in Chelsea attackers: they have conceded 4.86 expected goals across the opening three Gameweeks and remain a side to target. Elsewhere, Mameadu Sangari’s half-time withdrawal after a yellow card is frustrating but not enough to force a sale at £5.7m; owners can bench him or monitor his minutes, while non-owners should avoid buying before difficult fixtures against Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool. Nathan Collins’ calf injury could improve Ajer’s Brentford minutes, but Brentford defenders are not immediate targets because their next four fixtures are tough.
key_points: Transfer priority: move Rayan Cherki to Morgan Rogers for Gameweek 4 if chasing Chelsea’s Hull fixture and Rogers’ expected price rise.
Sell Phil Foden more readily than Cherki, as Foden’s benching makes his starts uncertain; wait for Manchester City’s Champions League news before acting.
Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweeks 5 and 7, while Joao Pedro is a strong Gameweek 4 play against Hull.
Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are safe holds despite Manchester City, but Fernandes to Cole Palmer or Mbeumo to Rogers is a valid upside move.
Do not rush to sell injured Nico O’Reilly unless he is ruled out for several weeks; benching him in Gameweek 4 and reassessing for Sunderland is viable.
Arsenal’s Kiwior at £4.4m is a strong defensive value pick while Mosquera is unavailable, with a likely starting role through Gameweek 10.
Avoid buying Mameadu Sangari after his half-time substitution until his role is clearer, though existing owners need not panic-sell.
Continue targeting Hull with Chelsea attackers despite their early clean sheets, as their expected-goals-conceded numbers suggest defensive regression.

items.title: 72 POINTS SO FAR! 🚀 | FPL CHAI'S GW4 TEAM REVEAL! 🚨 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Cole Palmer becomes the priority as Foden’s City minutes undermine Chai’s Gameweek 4 plan
items.summary:
Chai sits on 72 points before Chelsea v Arsenal and Manchester United v Everton, boosted by a Triple Captain return from Erling Haaland and points from Liverpool trio Virgil van Dijk, Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexander Isak. His Gameweek 3 patience with double Tottenham defence also pays off, although Spurs are fortunate to keep a clean sheet against Nottingham Forest. Isak’s goal and early substitution are not a concern in isolation, but his Champions League workload ahead of Fulham at home needs monitoring.

The main Gameweek 4 priority is finding a route to Cole Palmer. Palmer looks central to Chelsea’s attack, plays with freedom, has secure minutes and offers a captaincy option for several weeks. Chai is unwilling to go without him even if Chelsea face Arsenal, and rates Palmer as a stronger medium-term pick than Bruno Fernandes. Managers with Bruno are advised to consider moving to Palmer regardless of Bruno’s result against Everton, with Fernandes still a viable future buy when Manchester United’s fixtures improve.

Chai’s own squad has two free transfers and £1m in the bank, but the clean route of Harry Maguire down to a cheap defender and Antoine Semenyo up to Palmer is not convincing. The available defenders around £4.5m-£4.9m, including Crystal Palace’s Chris Richards, Leeds options and Newcastle’s Dan Burn, do not appeal enough to justify the move. Selling bench midfielder Solace to fund Palmer would leave too weak a bench and could force starts for Joe Gomez against Arsenal or Maguire against Manchester City.

Phil Foden is the other major dilemma after another reduced role for Manchester City, with Rayan Cherki competing for attacking minutes. Chai is tempted to keep Foden for the Manchester derby because of his quality, history in the fixture and the possibility that his tactical discipline earns him a start, but accepts City midfielders are becoming difficult to trust. Semenyo appears the safest City attacker for minutes and remains dangerous despite being used wide at times. No transfer should be made early, however: Champions League fixtures for Liverpool, City, Arsenal and others could bring injuries, rotation clues and decisive information before the deadline.

Wildcard managers can reasonably target Gameweek 4, using the European matches to assess City and Arsenal selection. Chelsea’s attack is attractive enough to support a triple-up, while Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is favoured over Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez because Arsenal have the better clean-sheet outlook and Raya offers reliable long-term minutes. Morgan Gibbs-White is also endorsed as a secure, penalty-taking Forest differential, while Newcastle’s Johan Wissa is a buy rather than a trap at £6.2m given his likely penalties, minutes and upcoming Leeds away and Hull at home fixtures.
key_points: Prioritise Cole Palmer for Gameweek 4, with captaincy viable against Hull at home and in subsequent weeks.
Do not make early transfers before the Champions League programme, especially with Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal assets vulnerable to rotation or injury news.
Phil Foden is an increasingly risky hold because of competition from Rayan Cherki, although the Manchester derby gives him one final case to retain.
Alexander Isak remains a hold for Fulham at home unless Liverpool’s European line-up raises major concerns over his minutes.
Avoid forcing Maguire to a £4.5m defender solely to fund Palmer; the current budget-defender market lacks a standout short-term option.
Wildcard squads can favour David Raya and Morgan Gibbs-White over Emiliano Martinez and Bukayo Saka for security of minutes and long-term structure.
Johan Wissa is a recommended Newcastle forward at £6.2m, with penalties, likely 90-minute outings and favourable fixtures supporting the pick.
Cole Palmer is preferred to Bruno Fernandes as a premium midfield transfer, while Bruno can be revisited for Manchester United’s later fixture run.

items.title: FPL GW3 DEADLINE LIVE! ⏰ GW3 Chips Active & Team News 🚨 | Get Your Last Minute FPL Questions In!
items.headline: Haaland Triple Captain Is the Call as Gameweek 3 Wildcard FOMO Builds
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout Gameweek 3 captain and the preferred Triple Captain choice for Manchester City’s home match against Coventry. The case is not simply Coventry’s newly promoted status: City have had an unusually long rest before the fixture, reducing the immediate rotation risk, whereas later Haaland opportunities against Ipswich and Hull come amid more fixture congestion and carry greater injury, rotation and opponent-improvement uncertainty. Ipswich may be marginally weaker on current evidence, but the recommendation is to take the premium fixture in front of you rather than wait for a theoretically better one.

Managers who already own Haaland are urged not to wildcard in Gameweek 3 simply because others are doing so to acquire him. The Gameweek 3 wildcard strategy often forces expensive Chelsea players such as Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro onto the bench for Arsenal away, while also encouraging short-term City picks, Arsenal defenders and uncertain options who will require swift exits. That can leave wildcard teams weaker for the immediate week and overloaded with future problems. A Gameweek 4 wildcard is preferred for a Haaland-owning squad that is not structurally set for the next fixture swing, particularly one carrying weak defenders or lacking Chelsea coverage.

For immediate transfers, Antoine Semenyo or Bryan Mbeumo to Rayan Cherki is the favoured move for managers targeting City’s Coventry fixture, with Phil Foden a viable cheaper alternative. Cherki is preferred on form and eye test despite some minutes risk, while Foden posts strong underlying numbers and is likely to start. City’s non-Haaland assets remain subject to rotation, however, with Nico O’Reilly the most questionable starter; early substitutions are also possible if City establish a comfortable lead. Josko Gvardiol offers greater defensive security than O’Reilly, while the appeal of Bernardo Silva at right-back is his defensive-contribution potential alongside penalties and set pieces.

Bench decisions are squad-dependent, but Joao Pedro is not an automatic starter at Arsenal. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is slightly preferred for one week because of his penalty appeal and a kinder matchup, especially for managers without Brighton defenders. Pascal Gross, Thiago and Brentford’s Kevin Schade are strong starters, while Solly March is worth retaining or starting if necessary rather than panic-selling after one poor half against Aston Villa. March’s Gameweek 1 output and Arsenal’s need for his defensive work against Chelsea still give him upside, although his minutes are not secure. Brighton’s Gomez, Sunderland defenders such as Dan Ballard and uncertain starters such as Ezri Konsa sit lower in the pecking order.

Liverpool’s late team news points to Jeremie Frimpong being benched, with Dominik Szoboszlai operating in midfield and Arne Slot’s side using a changed shape. Cody Gakpo is acceptable as a short-term aggressive punt, particularly on a Free Hit, but is not recommended as a long-term wildcard selection because Liverpool’s returning and new attacking options could soon affect his minutes. Similar caution applies to new arrivals such as Enzo, who is not expected to start immediately and needs a defined City role before becoming an FPL target.
key_points: Triple Captain Haaland against Coventry at home in Gameweek 3 rather than wait for Ipswich or Hull fixtures later in the season.
If you already own Haaland, avoid a Gameweek 3 wildcard unless your squad genuinely needs it; preserving the chip for Gameweek 4 is usually stronger.
Mbeumo or Semenyo to Cherki is the preferred short-term City move, with Foden a credible £0.5m cheaper alternative.
O’Reilly is the City starter with the greatest selection risk, while Gvardiol is safer for minutes and Bernardo Silva at right-back has defensive-contribution appeal.
Calvert-Lewin is marginally preferred to Joao Pedro this week, but Pedro remains an excellent season-long value asset rather than a sell.
Start Gross and Schade where possible; bench lower-ceiling or uncertain options such as Gomez, Hume, Ballard and Ndiaye first.
Do not overreact to March’s Gameweek 2 blank and half-time substitution: he is not nailed, but remains a reasonable hold or start against Chelsea.
Gakpo is a short-term Free Hit punt rather than a long-term wildcard pick, and Frimpong is expected to be on Liverpool’s bench.

items.title: WILDCARD ACTIVE! 🚨 FPL DEADLINE LIVE STREAM 🔴 FINAL TEAM! 🔒
items.headline: Foden gamble leads Gameweek 3 wildcard as Palmer move is booked for Gameweek 4
items.summary:
A Gameweek 3 wildcard is built around Erling Haaland captaincy at home to Coventry, with Phil Foden preferred to Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo for Manchester City’s standout fixture. Foden is vice-captain and is viewed as a one-week upside play: his underlying numbers are stronger than Cherki’s, while his expected minutes may be marginally safer. Cherki carries the greater ownership threat after his recent brace, but his minutes remain uncertain with Enzo Fernandez available, so Foden is the lower-owned calculated risk rather than a long-term hold.

The starting XI is Raya; Van Hecke, Chiao and De Cuyper; Gross, Szoboszlai, Foden, Saka and Sangaré; Haaland and Wissa. João Pedro, Concer, Mendy and Bentley sit on the bench. João Pedro is benched for Arsenal away despite his form because it is the rare fixture in which his high ownership can reasonably be opposed. Haaland remains the automatic captain against Coventry, while a triple-captain on him is considered viable but unavailable alongside an active wildcard; later home matches against Ipswich and Hull are alternative chip opportunities.

Bukayo Saka gets the Arsenal premium slot over Gabriel because the wildcard cannot comfortably accommodate Saka, Gabriel, Palmer and Haaland together. Saka’s penalty potential and attacking ceiling make him the preferred route, especially with favourable fixtures including Sunderland, Brighton, Leeds and Everton ahead. The plan is already set to sell Foden for Cole Palmer in Gameweek 4, restoring Chelsea coverage for Hull at home and likely handing Palmer the captaincy. The cash retained after that move is deliberately kept as protection against defensive problems rather than spent immediately.

De Cuyper is a short-term pick while Mitoma is sidelined until after the international break, with the expectation that he starts on the left in three of the next four Gameweeks. Van Hecke is selected as a £4.9m longer-term defender despite Brighton’s difficult immediate fixture, based on a strong schedule and the belief that their early defensive results overstate their weakness. Concer is benched against Chelsea but backed to become a regular Arsenal starter; if that call proves wrong, spare funds allow a switch to a £5.0m defender. Mendy is the budget defensive-contributions punt, with his early substitutions attributed to a lack of pre-season rather than a loss of status.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Coventry, with Foden as vice-captain; triple-captain Haaland is viable but is saved because the wildcard is active.
Foden edges Cherki and Semenyo as a one-week Manchester City punt, with greater upside and potentially steadier minutes despite Cherki’s much higher ownership.
Foden is booked to become Palmer in Gameweek 4, targeting Chelsea’s home fixture against Hull and Palmer captaincy.
Saka is chosen over Gabriel as the Arsenal premium because penalties and attacking upside outweigh the clean-sheet route when Haaland and Palmer are also required.
João Pedro is benched for Arsenal away, while Concer is also benched against Chelsea amid uncertainty over his immediate starting role.
De Cuyper is an out-of-position short-term option while Mitoma is injured, but retained bank funds provide an exit route when Mitoma returns.
Van Hecke is a long-term £4.9m defensive pick, while Sangaré is valued as a set-and-forget midfield option because of his strong defensive-contributions potential.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 3 Deadline Stream 🚀 Wildcard ACTIVE ✅
items.headline: Raya over Saka as Gameweek 3 wildcard backs Haaland without the Triple Captain chip
items.summary:
The Gameweek 3 wildcard settles on an Arsenal defensive route rather than Bukayo Saka, with David Raya preferred as the long-term set-and-forget goalkeeper. The decisive trade-off is Raya plus Manchester City midfielder Rayan Cherki, with a planned switch to Aston Villa’s Morgan Rogers in Gameweek 4, rather than Saka plus a cheaper goalkeeper. Saka’s penalty and set-piece appeal is acknowledged, but Arsenal’s Champions League schedule raises rotation concerns around fixtures such as Sunderland in Gameweek 4 and Hull in Gameweek 10.

Erling Haaland remains the central captaincy pick for Manchester City’s home fixture against Coventry, although the Triple Captain chip is held. Haaland is viewed as the standout captain and a viable Triple Captain option for managers not using another chip, because he is fit and has an exceptional fixture. However, there is reluctance to commit the chip while wildcarding, and a hope that his heavy Triple Captain ownership does not create a damaging rank swing. A future home match against Ipswich is considered only marginally better on paper and not necessarily worth waiting for.

The final squad leans on Raya, Riccardo Calafiori, Lewis Hall, Jan Paul van Hecke/Dikeper-type short-term defensive value, Ezri Konsa and Josko Gvardiol, while accepting uncertainty over several cheaper defenders’ minutes. Gvardiol is selected as a short-term City option despite the perennial Pep Guardiola rotation risk, with money retained in the bank to move a cheap defender up to a more reliable £5.0m option if required. Calafiori is valued for attacking upside but is not treated as permanently immune to rotation once European football intensifies.

In midfield, Cole Palmer stays despite Arsenal away, with Cherki chosen for Coventry before the likely Gameweek 4 move to Rogers. Dominik Szoboszlai is favoured over Liverpool’s more explosive but less secure attacking options because of his expected minutes, set pieces and potential defensive-contribution points. João Pedro is benched for Chelsea’s trip to Arsenal, while the forward line also includes Haaland and Igor Thiago/Wissa-type Brentford coverage. The overall aim is to avoid booking multiple early transfers, preserve flexibility and use the wildcard to create a stable base rather than chase every one-week punt.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland against Coventry in Gameweek 3; he is also the leading Triple Captain candidate for managers not using a wildcard or Free Hit.
Use the wildcard on Raya rather than Saka, as Raya offers secure long-term Arsenal coverage while Saka faces Champions League-related rotation risk.
Keep Cole Palmer through Arsenal away, with his penalties and season-long upside outweighing the difficult immediate fixture.
Start Cherki for Coventry at home, then target a Gameweek 4 transfer to Morgan Rogers for Aston Villa’s fixture against Hull.
Bench João Pedro in Gameweek 3 rather than Palmer, given Chelsea’s trip to Arsenal.
Gvardiol is a high-upside short-term City defender, but his minutes beyond Gameweek 3 are uncertain and should be monitored.
Avoid an overly fragile defence built around multiple £4.0m defenders; retain funds for a later upgrade to a dependable £5.0m defender.
Managers with Haaland and otherwise sound squads do not need to wildcard purely through fear of missing out; rolling transfers remains valuable.

items.title: FPL GW3 LIVE DEADLINE STREAM 📸 | TRIPLE CAPTAIN HAALAND! 🇳🇴 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Haaland Triple-Captain Backs City, but Cherki FOMO Does Not Force a Transfer
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is triple-captained for Gameweek 3 as Manchester City host Coventry, a fixture carrying an enormous goals projection after Coventry’s poor defensive start. Haaland is preferred to City midfield punts because, if City score heavily, he remains the likeliest top scorer. The chip is used now rather than saved for Haaland’s Gameweek 7 meeting with Ipswich because that later fixture follows Liverpool and PSG, creating greater fatigue and rotation risk. There is no guaranteed Double Gameweek before the first set of chips expires, so waiting is not automatically superior.

Despite strong temptation to buy Rayan Cherki or Phil Foden, the transfer is rolled. Bryan Mbeumo to Cherki is viewed as the obvious one-week upgrade for Coventry at home, but Mbeumo is the safer medium-term asset and Cherki’s place becomes less secure once Doku returns. Foden, Cherki and Semenyo are all expected to start this week, but City’s attacking options and upcoming Champions League schedule make them risky long-term holds; Semenyo is the safest for minutes but costs more. A move for Foden would also require downgrading the defence, which weakens the squad for Gameweeks 4-6.

The retained transfer is valued as future flexibility, particularly with Joe Rodon injured for around 10 weeks and a weak bench needing attention from Gameweek 4. Rodon can remain benched for now because he is not needed this week, while possible Gameweek 4 plans include Bruno Fernandes to Cole Palmer, Solace to Morgan Gibbs-White or Pascal Gross, and a defensive upgrade. A Wildcard in Gameweek 4 or 6 remains open, as does a Free Hit in Gameweek 4 if the combination of triple Manchester United, limited Chelsea coverage and defensive issues becomes too difficult to navigate.

Arsenal selection news creates further caution. Mosquera is only expected to train on Saturday after a precautionary absence, while new signing Ezri Konsa may start against Chelsea even if Mosquera is fit; Konsa is acceptable as a Wildcard bench option but not a defender to rely on immediately. Ben White should start in Gameweek 3, although Timber’s return soon adds future minutes risk. Solace is a hold if bench cover exists, but is not trusted to start or exceed 60 minutes after Eze’s encouraging appearance. Gross is the standout budget midfield replacement while Hinshelwood is absent, with a more advanced role making him preferable to pricier alternatives such as Jarrad Branthwaite Hall or short-term Brentford punts.
key_points: Triple-captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 3, with Coventry at home offering a stronger immediate setup than the rotation-prone Ipswich fixture in Gameweek 7.
Roll the transfer rather than forcing Mbeumo to Cherki or Solace to Foden; City midfielders are attractive for one week but carry major long-term minutes risk.
If making aggressive short-term moves before a Gameweek 4 Wildcard, Mbeumo to Cherki and Rodon to De Cuyper are the preferred pair.
Rodon is sidelined for roughly 10 weeks but can stay on the bench in Gameweek 3; his replacement is a priority from Gameweek 4.
Bench or sell Solace if possible, as his Arsenal start against Chelsea is uncertain; start dependable alternatives such as Dominic Calvert-Lewin, João Pedro or Gross instead.
Pascal Gross is the preferred sub-£7m midfielder for Gameweek 3, especially with an advanced role while Hinshelwood is injured.
Avoid buying Ben White now despite an expected Gameweek 3 start, as Timber’s return could affect his minutes from Gameweek 4 onwards.
A Gameweek 3 Free Hit should heavily target Manchester City, Liverpool and Brentford, with Haaland, Cherki, Foden and at least two Brentford defenders among the main considerations.

items.headline: Tino Barry gains FPL appeal as Everton’s unchallenged striker and possible penalty taker
items.summary:
Tino Barry emerges as one of the more interesting forward options after Everton fail to add a recognised striker before the deadline. With no direct positional rival, Barry is set for sustained minutes and may also take penalties following Iliman Ndiaye’s departure; he took Everton’s latest pre-season spot-kick, although James Garner remains a possible alternative. That security makes Barry especially appealing to wildcard managers, while Brentford’s Thiago is a strong Free Hit pick for Sunderland at home after scoring twice in the equivalent fixture last season.

Manchester City’s home match against Coventry is a major FPL focus, with Erling Haaland expected to lead the line against the promoted side. Enzo Fernandez is available following his move but may begin on the bench after limited recent minutes, while Iliman Ndiaye is also likely to be eased in. Nico O’Reilly should retain his place for now because of his penalty-box threat, but Fernandez’s arrival creates a longer-term minutes risk. Savinho can cover Haaland centrally if needed, and Ndiaye could then operate from the left, adding further uncertainty to City’s attacking selection once the Champions League begins.

Short-term defensive opportunities are concentrated around Brighton and Arsenal. Brighton’s Kaoru Mitoma remains sidelined until after the international break, leaving Diego Gomez as an out-of-position option for at least three more gameweeks; he suits managers planning to wildcard in Gameweek 6. Brighton face Leeds, who lose Joe Rodon for eight to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury. Arsenal’s Cristhian Mosquera is doubtful after missing training despite Mikel Arteta calling his issue precautionary, potentially opening the door for Piero Hincapie to start against Chelsea. Jurrien Timber is back in training but is at best a bench option.

Several new signings carry immediate selection caveats. Liverpool’s Bradley Barcola and Newcastle’s Fernandez are in their squads but lack match fitness and are more likely to be substitutes. Nottingham Forest’s Daniel Munoz and Liam Delap are also not fully up to speed, with Munoz particularly likely to be managed after surgery and limited pre-season minutes. Spurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk is available but is expected to manage only 15 to 20 minutes, while James Maddison and Savinho return to training. Crystal Palace’s Ismaila Sarr remains a major concern after his collapsed Liverpool move, with a groin issue officially cited and no expectation of an imminent return; Jean-Philippe Mateta is also out until after the international break.
key_points: Captaincy attention naturally falls on Erling Haaland at home to Coventry, although Manchester City’s supporting attackers face growing rotation risk.
Tino Barry is a wildcard forward candidate because Everton have no specialist striker to displace him and he could inherit penalty duties.
Thiago is a leading Free Hit option for Brentford’s home fixture against Sunderland after scoring twice in this match-up last season.
Diego Gomez remains an out-of-position Brighton option until at least after the international break, with Mitoma still unavailable.
Joe Rodon is out for eight to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury and needs to be sold by FPL managers.
Brentford’s Kristoffer Ajer is useful for the immediate fixture but is less attractive as a long-term wildcard pick because Sepp van den Berg is nearing a post-break return.
Daniel Munoz, Liam Delap, Bradley Barcola, Newcastle’s Fernandez and Enzo Fernandez are available but may be limited to substitute appearances because of match fitness.
Crystal Palace’s Sarr, Mateta and Chadi Riad remain unavailable, while Arsenal’s Mosquera is a doubt and could hand Hincapie a start against Chelsea.

items.headline: Rodon injury forces defensive rethink as City moves tempt Bruno and Mbeumo sales
items.summary:
The squad is broadly in good shape, but the lack of Manchester City coverage becomes a growing concern after delaying an early transfer. Bringing in another City player appears to require a significant sacrifice, with Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo the two premium midfielders who could be sold, while a cheaper route involving Solis is also under consideration.

Joe Rodon’s injury creates the more immediate problem. He was due to be relied upon in Gameweeks 4 and 5, but his absence leaves the defence short of playable options and reduces cover over the next two rounds. That makes fixing the back line a priority rather than simply chasing additional City assets.

A Solis-to-Rodon move would require finding an extra £0.5m elsewhere. Harry Maguire or Rodon are the obvious potential sources of funds, but replacing Rodon with John Egan is not viewed as a convincing long-term solution: it may make the numbers work, yet it does little to solve the wider defensive weakness. The central decision is whether to protect key midfield assets and patch the defence cheaply, or sell Bruno or Mbeumo to open a more meaningful route into Manchester City.
key_points: Joe Rodon’s injury leaves the squad with limited defensive cover for Gameweeks 4 and 5.
Manchester City coverage is the main transfer concern after no early move is made.
Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are the leading sale candidates if funds are needed for another City player.
A Solis-to-Rodon transfer needs £0.5m to be freed elsewhere.
Selling Harry Maguire or Rodon could create the required money, but a John Egan replacement is not considered a durable defensive fix.
The key trade-off is between retaining Bruno and Mbeumo or restructuring midfield to solve both City coverage and defensive depth.

Start Bart Verbruggen over Antonín Kinský because Tottenham's defensive start makes Kinský a weak option.
Play Calafiori, Aké and Maguire in defence, while injured Joe Rodon and Diop stay on the bench.

items.headline: Haaland captains Andy’s Gameweek 3 Wildcard as Palmer faces Arsenal bench call
items.summary:
Andy plans to activate his Wildcard for Gameweek 3 after confirmation that Erling Haaland trains and is fit, with Haaland an automatic captain for Manchester City’s trip to Coventry. His preferred core includes Haaland, Joao Pedro and Wissa up front, plus Cole Palmer, Dominik Szoboszlai, Pascal Gross and Sangare in midfield. He views Joao Pedro as underpriced at £7.5m and Wissa as excellent value, while Gross’s penalties and set pieces and Sangare’s defensive-contribution potential make them reliable budget options even when they are only bench cover.

The biggest immediate dilemma is whether to start Chelsea’s Palmer or Joao Pedro away to Arsenal. Andy strongly rates Arsenal’s clean-sheet prospects despite Chelsea’s attacking quality, and is currently inclined to bench Joao Pedro while starting Palmer because Palmer has penalties and offers a higher ceiling. He accepts that benching the heavily owned Joao Pedro is risky, but considers Arsenal away one of the toughest fixtures available. Looking beyond Gameweek 3, he likes a triple Chelsea attack of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers from Gameweek 4, when Chelsea’s schedule improves markedly; if he starts with a Manchester City punt such as Rayan Cherki, he expects to move Cherki to Rogers next week.

Szoboszlai remains a hold despite likely playing at right-back against Ipswich. Andy believes he retains set pieces, probable penalties, 90-minute security and potentially better defensive-contribution prospects, while still having licence to get forward. Florian Wirtz is the more appealing short-term Free Hit punt, but Szoboszlai is preferred over the longer term because his role should eventually return to midfield. Cody Gakpo is an attractive short-term differential for Ipswich, but the arrival of Barcola reduces his long-term minutes security.

In defence, Andy wants Arsenal coverage through Raya and Riccardo Calafiori, with Kiwior/Konza a cheap £4.4m route if Mosquera is ruled out or limited. Lewis Hall is his favoured Newcastle defender over Dedic for longer-term attacking upside, although Dedic is acceptable as a £4.5m short-term pick while Livramento is absent. He also likes De Cuyper as a defender playing left wing for Brighton, particularly if Mitoma’s absence proves prolonged. His final Wildcard choice centres on whether to use Cherki and a more attacking Manchester City defender such as O’Reilly, or instead choose Bukayo Saka, Gvardiol and cheaper rotating goalkeepers. Saka is a major differential but carries Champions League rotation risk.

Managers intending to Wildcard in Gameweek 4 do not need to spend transfers simply because they have them, since free transfers now carry over through the chip. However, Andy thinks one short-term move into Manchester City’s Coventry fixture, such as Bryan Mbeumo to Cherki or Phil Foden, can be justified before restructuring for Chelsea in Gameweek 4. He advises holding Dango Ouattara for Sunderland at home if he must be started, or ideally benching him for another week of team-news clarity, as there are no obvious sub-£6.5m midfield replacements that demand an immediate transfer.
key_points: Erling Haaland is fit, is Andy’s Gameweek 3 captain and is central to his active Wildcard draft for Coventry away.
Cole Palmer is marginally preferred to Joao Pedro for the starting XI against Arsenal because of penalties, although both are strong longer-term Chelsea assets.
A triple Chelsea attack of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers is viable from Gameweek 4 despite the poor Arsenal fixture in Gameweek 3.
Dominik Szoboszlai remains a hold even if he starts at right-back against Ipswich, due to set pieces, likely penalties, minutes and defensive-contribution potential.
Kiwior/Konza becomes an appealing £4.4m Arsenal defensive pick if Mosquera is unavailable, but is not a transfer to force without confirmed team news.
Lewis Hall is the preferred Newcastle defender for long-term upside; Dedic is a reasonable £4.5m short-term alternative while Livramento is out.
De Cuyper’s value rises if Mitoma, Minteh and other Brighton wide options remain absent, as he should continue at left wing.
Managers Wildcarding in Gameweek 4 can preserve transfers, but a one-week Manchester City move such as Mbeumo to Cherki or Foden is worth considering for Coventry.

Calvert-Lewin is kept in the XI in the hope that he can sustain that form.

The wider call is to avoid Chelsea attackers at the Emirates rather than force a player into the side on name value. Rushworth, Thomas and Van Ewijk complete the bench, leaving the team heavily committed to City’s upside while accepting uncertainty in the United defence and Calvert-Lewin’s fixture.

Ryan Cherki replaces Bryan Mbeumo, increasing exposure to Manchester City’s high-upside Coventry match.
Senne Lammens starts against Everton, with United’s shaky defence offset by Everton’s weak attacking output and Ndiaye’s absence.

items.headline: Haaland Triple Captain shapes Gameweek 3 plan as Cherki replaces Mbeumo
items.summary:
A 150-point Gameweek 2 has pushed the squad into the top 10 overall, but the approach remains deliberately measured: make one final aggressive move for Gameweek 3, then stabilise with a likely Wildcard in Gameweek 4. Bruno Fernandes is central to the current team after 23 points and an extremely advanced false-nine role alongside Cunha. Everton have conceded a high volume of big chances despite conceding only once, and with Ndiaye absent, Fernandes’ penalties, set pieces and shooting or creative routes make him a strong pick again.

The defence starts Calafiori, Ballard and Ajer, with Lammens in goal against Everton. Calafiori remains a standout because Arsenal offer clean-sheet potential while he routinely occupies attacking positions around and inside the opposition box; his two league assists and Community Shield goal underline that upside. Ballard is a weaker clean-sheet play away to Brentford, but Brentford’s direct style should generate clearances and interceptions, making defensive-contribution points a realistic cushion. Lammens is retained because Manchester United’s clean-sheet odds are broadly comparable with most available alternatives, while Everton’s depleted forward options improve the fixture.

In midfield, Fernandes, Szoboszlai, Schade and Pascal Gross all start. Szoboszlai has Ipswich and offers defensive contributions alongside set pieces and potential penalties, while Schade is backed as Brentford’s in-form, secure starter for Sunderland at home. Gross is trusted for 90 minutes, penalties and corners despite overperforming in Gameweek 2. João Pedro is benched against Arsenal away: Chelsea are projected for only 1.02 goals, making his attacking ceiling too low relative to the alternatives, even if benching an in-form player carries some risk.

The key transfer is Bryan Mbeumo out for Rayan Cherki, adding a second Manchester City attacker alongside Erling Haaland for Coventry at home. Cherki’s chance creation, shooting quality and recent decisive performances make him preferable to Phil Foden, while new signings are not expected to immediately displace City’s established starters. Haaland is captain and is close to a locked Triple Captain: City’s projected 2.96 goals offer one of the season’s biggest attacking opportunities, Coventry look vulnerable after two defeats, and Haaland is fit, rested and in form. The alternative Triple Captain fixtures, Ipswich at home in Gameweek 7 and Hull at home in Gameweek 16, carry more uncertainty around form, fitness, fatigue and Hull’s defensive resilience.

A Gameweek 4 Wildcard is strongly considered because the current squad has structural problems beyond this week: Coventry assets have disappointed, Ballard’s fixtures worsen, the Manchester United contingent faces Manchester City, and the squad lacks sufficient Chelsea and Arsenal coverage. The plan is therefore to maximise City’s Coventry fixture now, gather one more week of information, then rebuild for the fixture changes.
key_points: Triple Captain Erling Haaland is the preferred Gameweek 3 chip, with Manchester City projected for 2.96 goals at home to Coventry.
Rayan Cherki replaces Bryan Mbeumo, providing additional Manchester City attacking exposure after two price rises.
Bruno Fernandes remains a major Gameweek 3 pick against Everton because of his false-nine positioning, penalties and Everton’s poor chance concession data.
João Pedro is benched against Arsenal away, with Chelsea projected for only 1.02 goals in their hardest fixture of the season.
Calafiori starts for Arsenal because his advanced role combines strong attacking involvement with reliable clean-sheet potential.
Ballard starts despite only a 16% Sunderland clean-sheet chance, as Brentford’s direct play should offer defensive-contribution points.
A Gameweek 4 Wildcard is likely to address weak Coventry assets and add more Chelsea and Arsenal coverage.
